peoples.name: Ardenians — 72%
peoples.body: The national majority is strongest in Anera and the Sela and less settled in the industrial east and coastal south. The figure comes from a 1989 census taken by an authority nobody now trusts.

peoples.name: Kolvenians — 14%
peoples.body: Union-era industrial settlement made Kolvenian-speakers a plurality in Zavost's cities. They are disproportionately young, qualified and likely to have left since independence, through a border that went uncounted for two years.

peoples.name: Vetreni — 7%
peoples.body: Almost all Vetreni now live beyond the ceasefire line. Their dialect and history of autonomy are distinct; their relationship to Ardenia has rarely been one of uncomplicated consent.

peoples.name: Tavri Muslims — 4%
peoples.body: An urban and mercantile southern community present since the Sarine period. It has supported every government since independence in exchange for being left alone.

peoples.name: Others — 3%
peoples.body: Sela Roma, a residual Aurine-descended merchant community in Tavri, and the remainder produced by an obsolete census.

demography.name: The demography of collapse
demography.body: The birth rate has halved since 1989. Somewhere between 200,000 and 400,000 people have left since independence, disproportionately the young, the qualified and the Kolvenian. Male life expectancy has fallen by four years since 1990, a statistic about alcohol and despair rather than medicine.

social_order.name: The transition's winners
social_order.body: A small stratum did extremely well when state assets became sellable: Union-era plant directors, foreign-trade officials and the Falcons.

social_order.name: The professional class
social_order.body: Doctors, teachers and administrators have been comprehensively wiped out. A Vashtera doctor's monthly salary buys less than a coastal customs clerk earns off the books in a week.

social_order.name: The industrial workforce
social_order.body: Zavost's workers remain employed on paper by enterprises that have not paid wages in four months. They retain scarce skills, real unions and the capacity to stop the eastern economy.

social_order.name: The countryside
social_order.body: The countryside has land and no credit, and is eating better than the towns for the first time in seventy years.

social_order.name: The pension cohort
social_order.body: Some 1.1 million people saw their life savings erased by the ruble's collapse in 1991. They vote at nearly ninety per cent.

language_and_script.name: Language and script
language_and_script.body: Ardenian is written in the Verzhan alphabet standardised by the Lamplight writers in the 1860s. The Union imposed a Kolvenian-based official script in 1938; the Assembly restored Verzhan in 1990. The working administration reads the other alphabet more fluently, while textbooks, land registers, criminal files, pension rolls and old deeds sit in three scripts without a concordance. This is not merely a cultural grievance. It is why land reform cannot be executed.

religion.name: The Ardenian Apostolic Church
religion.body: Autocephalous and claiming a ninth-century foundation, the Church is the country's most trusted institution. The Union shut its seminaries in 1929 and a Patriarch died in custody in 1937, then domesticated the surviving hierarchy through appointments vetted by the Third Directorate. It organises Anera, could contain or legitimise the Vasca remnant, opposes recognition of Vetrenka and the loss of twelve monasteries beyond the line, and holds views on schools, script and the seventy per cent of its pre-1921 property now serving as sanatoria or tractor depots.

religion.name: The Kolvenian Orthodox Exarchate
religion.body: The Exarchate serves most of Zavost and answers to a synod in Krasova. The National Conservatives want it expelled; doing so would radicalise the industrial east and give Krasova an enduring international grievance.

religion.name: The Tavri Muslim community
religion.body: Four per cent of the country, urban, mercantile and studiedly unaligned. Its arrangement with the state remains stable precisely while nobody turns it into a symbol.

religion.name: The irreligious third
religion.body: Roughly a third of Ardenia is functionally irreligious, a Union-era inheritance concentrated in Zavost and the Vashtera professional class.
